body_opening:
DeepSeek-V4.1 stores its compressed KV as NVFP4 (288 B/token: 512 e2m1 values packed two per byte, then 32 e4m3 scales of 16 dims each) next to an fp8 sliding-window cache. # HISA: Hierarchical Sparse Attention for DeepSeek-V3.2 DSA



## Motivation

This PR adds **HISA (Hierarchical Indexed Sparse Attention)**, an alternative implementation of the DSA (DeepSeek Sparse Attention) indexer used by DeepSeek-V3.2, gated behind a model-config flag.

HISA replaces DSA's dense per-token indexer score computation with a two-stage hierarchical shortlist:

- **Stage 1 — coarse block-level selection.** Group K tokens into pool blocks of `k_block_size`, mean-pool each block, then score each query against all pool blocks and pick the top `block_topk` blocks per query.
- **Stage 2 — fine-grained token-level scoring.** For each query, run a full-resolution fp8 MQA

Since we can't invoke these instructions directly from Python, a small Python extension is required.

title: [Kernel] Fuse KV-cache writes for asymmetric K/V (head_dim != v_head_dim)
body_opening:
MHATokenToKVPool gated the fused store_cache JIT kernel on head_dim == v_head_dim, so models with asymmetric KV (MiMo-V2.5 is 192/128) fell back to two separate index_put_ per layer. This specializes the kernel on (k_row_bytes, v_row_bytes) and gives K and V independent cache strides, so asymmetric K/V takes the fused path as well. Equal-width K/V keeps the existing interleaved two-tensor copy unchanged.

MiMo-V2.5 (310B) TP=4, bs=1 decode: KV-write kernels 102 -> 51 per step, KV-write GPU time -76%, output throughput +2.9%, generated tokens byte-identical.

Also tightens the CPU AMX path, which takes a single row_dim for both tensors and therefore only serves equal-width rows.
